2 08-01-2020 Learned counsel for the petitioner is permitted to write the complete description of the Food Inspector as shown in the prosecution report in course of the day.

Issue notice to opposite party no. 2 both by registered cover with A/D as well as ordinary process for which requisites etc. must be filed within one week from today, failing which this application shall stand dismissed without further reference to a Bench.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he has prayed for quashing of the order dated 15.04.2010 passed by learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhagalpur by which cognizance of the offence under Section 16(1)(a) of the Patna High Court CR.
dt.08-01-2020 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act has been taken and the petitioner has been summoned by the learned Magistrate.

In alternative the petitioner has also prayed for setting aside the order dated 08.02.2013 whereby the learned S.D.J.M., Bhagalpur has issued process under Section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the subsequent order dated 19.04.2018 by which Gulab Singh vs State Of Bihar Through Its Principal ... on 8 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98914760/
1 process under Section 83 Cr.P.C. has been taken out against the petitioner.

sentences.text:
It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is the President of M/s.
Balvikas Evam Paryavaran Samarak Sansthan whose registered office is at New Delhi.
It is a non-government organization and had entered into an agreement with the State of Bihar to serve mid day meal in the cluster schools.

On 21.04.2010, on the basis of a complaint lodged by the Civil Surgeon-cum-Chief Medical Officer, Bhagalpur alleging that in course of his inspection the Chana Dal did not confirm with the prescribed standard of quality and had been found to be adulterated,
the learned C.J.M. has taken cognizance and issued summons against the petitioner and other co-accused.

Learned counsel submits that the issuance of summon against the petitioner is in a routine and mechanical manner as Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.83740 of 2019(2) dt.08-01-2020 no material has been found against the petitioner to make out a prima-facie case against him so as to issue summons.

It is his submission that in the complaint petition nothing has been stated regarding the role of the petitioner and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a complaint case against a Company it was incumbent upon the complainant to indicate briefly as to how the accused is In-charge of and in ultimate control of the affairs of the company, in this case the N.G.O.
Learned counsel further submits that on perusal of the impugned order issuing process under Section 82 and 83 Cr.P.C. it would appear that those orders have been passed without being satisfied with the service report of summons or the execution of warrant as it is the case of the petitioner that neither any summon nor any warrant was ever served upon the petitioner.

Learned counsel has relied upon Section 87 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to submit that if the Court was willing to issue a warrant of arrest and process under Section 82 and 83 Cr.P.C. in addition to summons, the Court was required to record reasons as according to him Section 87 Cr.P.C. has been held to be a mandatory provision under the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.83740 of 2019(2) dt.08-01-2020 Learned APP for the State is present.

Taking not of the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, this Court directs that till next date of hearing the process issued under Section 82 and 83 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the learned court below in P.S. Case No. 112 of 2010 corresponding to Trial No. 3134 of 2010 pending in the court of learned S.D.J.M., Bhagalpur shall remain stayed.
List this matter after six weeks on 24th February, 2020.

(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J)
